title: Reading ×, ÷, and = Symbols
keyIdea: The multiply sign × means equal groups (2 × 3 is two groups of three). The divide sign ÷ means share equally (6 ÷ 2 is 6 shared into 2 groups). The equals sign = means both sides have the same value — not only "write the answer on the right".
familyTip: Point at a packet of biscuits: "2 rows of 3 — that is 2 × 3." Share grapes into 2 plates and say "6 ÷ 2". Flip a true sentence: "5 = 2 + 3" is still true because both sides match.

visual.caption: Which sign? Drag each story, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match × ÷ = to their jobs, build an array, share equally, balance both sides, and pick the sign for a story.

kid: × means equal groups. 2 × 3 means 2 groups of 3. That is 3 and 3, which make 6.
÷ means share equally. 6 ÷ 2 means share 6 into 2 equal groups. Each group gets 3.
= means the same value. 4 + 2 = 6 is true because both sides are 6. 5 = 2 + 3 is also true.
Do not mix the signs. + adds. × makes equal groups. ÷ shares. = checks that both sides match.
adult: Year 2 maths: × means equal groups or an array. ÷ means share or split into equal groups. = means both sides have the same value. Words to use: multiply, divide, equal groups, array, share equally, same value, equals.
Common mistakes: reading × as + (2 × 3 as 5); treating ÷ as take away (6 ÷ 2 as 4); thinking = only means "write the answer on the right" so 5 = 2 + 3 looks wrong; swapping × and ÷ in a story.

In the lab your child matches each sign to its job, builds a 2-by-3 array, shares 8 into 4 equal groups, balances an equals sentence, picks the sign for a story, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

practice.hint: × makes equal groups. How many groups, and how many in each?
practice.explain: 2 × 3 is 2 groups of 3 (or 3 + 3). Adding would be 2 + 3 = 5. Sticking digits is not multiplying.

practice.hint: ÷ shares into equal groups. It is not the same as one subtraction.
practice.explain: 8 ÷ 2 shares 8 into 2 equal groups of 4. Taking away once is subtraction, not division.

practice.prompt: {a} groups of {b}. What total does {a} × {b} make?
practice.hint: Equal groups: add {b} again and again, {a} times — or multiply.

practice.prompt: Share {n} into {k} equal groups. How many in each group?
Which sentence is true because both sides match?
practice.hint: Check the value on each side. = needs the same value both sides.
practice.explain: 2 + 3 = 5, so 5 = 2 + 3 is true. 2 × 3 = 6 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so those do not match 5.

pool.hint: Think of bags of the same size, or rows in an array.
pool.explain: × means equal groups (or times). Take away is −. Writing an answer is not what × means.

pool.hint: Picture sweets split fairly onto plates.
pool.explain: ÷ shares or groups equally. Adding is +. Making bigger is not a named sign here.

choices: both sides have the same value
always put the answer on the right
pool.hint: Equals is a balance. Either side can be a sum or a product.
pool.explain: Equals means same value. 7 = 3 + 4 is fine. It is not only "answer goes right".

pool.prompt: 3 rows of 4 counters is best written as…
pool.hint: Rows of the same length are equal groups — that is multiply.
pool.explain: 3 × 4 is three groups of four. 3 + 4 is only seven. 3 ÷ 4 is not whole groups here.

pool.prompt: Which shows sharing, not grouping as rows?
pool.hint: Sharing uses ÷. Rows of equal size use ×.
pool.explain: 12 ÷ 3 shares 12 into 3 equal groups. 3 × 4 is equal groups as a product. 2 + 2 is add.

choices: the answer must sit on the left
pool.hint: Check the value of each side.
pool.explain: 2 × 3 = 6, so both sides match. Equals does not force the answer to the left; × is not add.
